heading: Dependencies point down
body:
A class needs another class when it names it: the type of a field, a `Needs` list, or the field name that `NeedsAll` reads, such as `orderStore` in JavaScript or `order_store` in Ruby and Python. Tachyon draws these needs as a graph for each realm and checks two things.

First, the needs point down, the same way in every app:

| Layer | Folder | May need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry point | `server/controllers`, and Tac views | Services, and the layers below |
| Service | `client/services`, `server/services` | Other services, helpers, stores, repositories and clients |
| Helper | `@Helper` classes in `client/helpers`, `server/helpers` | Other helpers, stores, repositories and clients, never a service |
| Data access | `stores`, `repositories`, `clients` | Other data access, never a service or a helper |
| Utility | `client/shared/utils`, `server/utils` | No role class (`TY1327`); every layer may call it |

Nothing may need a controller, because only a request calls a controller. A store must not need a service or a helper, because they use data access, not the other way round.

Second, no chain of needs loops back to where it started, even when each step points down. If `OrderService` needs `PaymentService` and `PaymentService` needs `OrderService`, neither can be built first, and neither owns the rule they share. This is the same as Spring Boot, which refuses circular references.

The build refuses either problem with `TY1327`. For a loop, the message names the whole loop, for example `Circular dependency: OrderService -> PaymentService -> OrderService`. To break a loop, move the code that the classes share into a new service that each of them uses, or let one class publish an event instead of calling back. To fix a store that needs a service, move the code that needs the service up into a service that uses the store.

This check is new, so you can turn it off for one side of the app while you move code. For Tac code, set `tac.dependencies.check` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon code, set `dependencies.check` to `false` in `server/application.json`. Use these settings only for migration. `ty migrate check` lists every place to change, even when the setting is off.
